title: Restriction of scalars length for a semilocal algebra
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative local ring, meaning a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and put $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism to a commutative ring whose set $X$ of maximal ideals is finite. Suppose every $\mathfrak q\in X$ contracts to $\mathfrak m$ and the induced field extension $k\to B/\mathfrak q$ has finite dimension $f_{\mathfrak q}=[B/\mathfrak q:k]$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Let $M$ be a $B$-module of finite length [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. For $\mathfrak q\in X$ write $B_{\mathfrak q}$ for the localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $M_{\mathfrak q}=(B\setminus\mathfrak q)^{-1}M$ for module localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then $M$ has finite length over $A$ by restriction of scalars and $$\mathrm{length}_A(M)=\sum_{\mathfrak q\in X}f_{\mathfrak q}\,\mathrm{length}_{B_{\mathfrak q}}(M_{\mathfrak q}).$$

source.place: Tag 02M0 (lemma-pushdown-module), statement and its simple-factor filtration proof.

proof.text: Induct on Mathlib IsFiniteLength, whose constructors give either a zero module or an extension of a previously handled finite-length submodule N by a simple quotient. This is the simple-factor induction of Stacks Tag 02M0 without separately choosing a composition series. In the zero case every localization is zero, so the assertion holds.

Identify the simple quotient Q with B/q for a maximal ideal q using isSimpleModule_iff_quot_maximal, then with q.ResidueField using the bijective canonical algebra map. Give this field the k=(maximalIdeal A).ResidueField action induced by Ideal.ResidueField.map. Its compatibility with the A-action is map_algebraMap. Surjectivity of A to k identifies A-length with k-length, and Module.length_eq_finrank gives the assumed finite residue degree.

At p=q, the identity map on q.ResidueField is a module localization map, since every denominator is a unit. IsLocalizedModule.iso identifies its localization with that field over B_q. The surjective local residue map shows its length is one. At p distinct from q, maximality gives an element a in q outside p. It annihilates the residue field and belongs to the denominator set, so LocalizedModule.subsingleton_iff makes its localization zero. Transport both calculations along the localized simple-quotient isomorphism.

Apply length additivity to 0 -> N -> M -> Q -> 0 after restriction to A. The induction hypothesis and finite residue degree show finite A-length. Localize the same exact sequence at each maximal p: localization preserves exactness, injectivity and surjectivity. Length additivity over B_p gives length(M_p)=length(N_p)+1 if p=q and length(N_p) otherwise. Distribute multiplication and the finite sum. Since q belongs to X, its one nonzero new summand is the residue degree. This proves the equality and completes the induction, including the zero-ring case.
